text.description: Follow the jeep road and use trail north along San Joaquin Ridge, with easy navigation and little elevation gain.
A non-technical class 2 ascent from the northwest; long approach via Lamarck Col, the John Muir Trail and Ionian Basin.

text.description: Follow an old road onto the Albanita Trail to a saddle on the northeast ridge, then go cross-country past a granite crag to the rocky summit. About 3.3 miles round trip with 1,100 ft of gain and a short exposed scramble at the end.
Climb the sandy scree to Longley Pass from the Cedar Grove side, then take class 3 rock to the summit, which sits on the west side of the ridge.

text.description: Hike the trail past Statham Meadow to the saddle near the Geraldine Lakes, then walk the easy ridge to the summit. The trail is faint in places.
Reach the Pacific Crest Trail saddle north of the summit, then climb the north ridge. Expect loose rock, side-hilling and tricky chute-finding on exposed third class.

name: Southeast Face from St. Marys Pass

text.description: Take the trail to St. Marys Pass, then north along the broad ridge until the trail fades at the saddle before the peak. Climb the south face of dirt, sand and scree, with some class 2 rock near the top.

text.description: Cross Shepherd Pass, drop to the Kern, and climb Milestone Basin to the base of the southeast face. A prominent ramp leads up the left side to a keyhole and the summit plateau, with the high point at its north end.

text.description: Take the Big Meadow Trail to the saddle at the head of Taylor Creek, follow the ridge to the base of the dome, and finish up a short chimney from the saddle. Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 3.
Follow the Birch Creek trail to Birch Lake, climb the steep ramp west of the lake to the crest, then ascend talus and snow to the summit. The ramp holds snow into summer and may need crampons.

text.description: Go up the Bubbs Creek and East Lake drainages past Lake Reflection to the lakes below Thunder Col, then climb the east ridge or southeast slopes. The summit crux is a short exposed move on the north summit block. Class 3 to the summit block, which is Class 4.

text.description: Reach the Pacific Crest Trail and follow it to the saddle just southeast of the peak, then walk a short distance to the summit. A longer, easier approach comes along the crest trail from Donner Pass.
Take the Blue Canyon Trail to its north end, continue up to Dykeman Pass, drop into the Alpine Creek drainage and climb talus to the east ridge. The ridge has some class 3 scrambling.

text.description: Climb the Mountaineers Route to the Russell-Carillon plateau, cross the Russell-Carillon pass (class 3 on the north side) to Tulainyo Lake, then walk the sandy south slopes to the summit.
